title: No two shortest routes tie before tau
claim: In the directed medial graph D of every regular tessellation {f, m} of the Euclidean or hyperbolic plane (vertices the edges of the tessellation, an arc for each corner from its edge to the next edge about its vertex): (1) for two routes P, Q with common ends meeting nowhere else, with the disc between them on P's left, km = I + d_P, jf = I + d_Q, I = k + j - 1 + n and n = k + j - 2 - p_F - q_V, so for equal lengths d = K(1 - 1/m - 1/f) + 1 - n with K = km = jf a common multiple of m and f; (2) a shortest route runs along each cell of that disc on its side at most once; (3) its ring runs have at most floor(m(f - 1)/f) arcs and its face runs at most floor(f(m - 1)/m); (4) hence no two different shortest routes with the same ends are shorter than tau = L - L/m - L/f + 1, L = lcm(m, f), so every contact within distance tau - 1 has a single shortest route and, over GF(2), (A^d)[x, y] = 1 at its distance d; (5) every closed route has length at least min(m, f), so for m = f the first tie is exactly at tau = m - 1. Computed: the first tie at tau on 42 hyperbolic covers (two primes each), and every pair of shortest routes read thin, at length c(tau - 1) + 1. Attainment of the tie at tau for m != f is computed, not proved.
failure_conditions: Two routes with common ends, meeting nowhere else, whose disc violates one of Theorem 1's counts.
A shortest route running along one cell of such a disc twice, or a ring or face run longer than its bound.
Two different shortest routes with the same ends in some {f, m}, shorter than tau.
A closed route shorter than min(m, f), or a type with m = f whose first tie is not at m - 1.
foundation_claim_scope: The contact graph of rule-60 rings on regular tessellations (rings at vertices, contacts at edges), given rather than grown; shortest routes and their ties (A40, A41). The covers are read in PSL(2, p).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's spawn on 2026-11-09.
validation.status: proof by hand (Theorems 1 to 3, Lemmas 1 and 2); the case analysis's arithmetic checked exactly; the covers computed
validation.novelty: new as far as found for directed routes; ingredients classical (combinatorial Gauss-Bonnet, thin bigons)
